surprises.description: UPS reported Q3 revenue of $22.9 billion versus the preview’s practical consensus bar of about $22.2 billion, and diluted EPS of $1.69 versus $1.62 consensus. Operating profit of $2.1 billion also exceeded the preview’s roughly $1.965 billion segment-based estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 consolidated revenue grew 6.7% year-over-year to $22.9 billion with operating profit of $2.1 billion and diluted EPS of $1.69, exceeding expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue consensus varies by vendor ... use $22.2B as the practical bar”; “Consensus Q3 EPS of $1.62”; the segment bridge estimated consolidated operating profit at “~$1,965M.”

surprises.description: International operating profit was expected to decline by about $23 million, but instead increased $55 million year over year; its 14.9% margin also topped the preview’s 13–14% guidance range. This happened despite an 8.7% decline in total volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International returned to year-over-year operating profit growth for the first time in 6 quarters, with profit up $55 million to $746 million and a 14.9% margin, even as total volume fell 8.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment bridge forecast International operating profit down “−$23M”; its Q3 framework listed an “International adj. op margin” of “13–14%.”

surprises.description: UPS raised its full-year 2026 outlook above the preview’s cited guide: revenue to about $92.6 billion from $91.2 billion, operating profit to $8.75 billion from $8.65 billion, and diluted EPS to about $7.28 from $7.22.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $92.6 billion in revenue, $8.75 billion in operating profit, and about $7.28 in diluted EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance treatment ($91.2B revenue / $8.65B adj. op profit / $7.22 adj. EPS).”

surprises.description: The Q4 revenue outlook of about $25.7 billion is above the roughly $24.9 billion the preview said was needed to meet the prior full-year revenue guide. The preview identified Q4 as heavily loaded, so this is a stronger revenue bridge than it had implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 guidance calls for revenue of ~$25.7 billion (up ~5%) and operating profit of ~$3.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With Q3 at consensus, Q4 must deliver ~$24.9B revenue and ~$2.77 EPS.”

surprises.description: UPS raised its full-year free-cash-flow forecast from $5.5 billion to about $6.1 billion and explicitly reaffirmed that the dividend is safe, improving the coverage picture the preview highlighted as a key risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow was raised to approximately $6.1 billion (including the $4 billion Driver Choice program payments) ... and management reaffirmed the dividend is safe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “FY FCF guide $5.5B vs. $5.4B of dividends (1.02x)” and said “Explicit dividend reaffirmation language matters as much as the EPS line.”

surprises.description: Supply Chain Solutions revenue reached $3 billion, above the preview’s roughly $2.75 billion estimate, with forwarding and logistics both growing strongly. The revenue strength contrasts with the segment’s weaker-than-expected operating result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Supply Chain Solutions revenue grew $459 million to $3 billion (forwarding up 17.5%, logistics up 17.2%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment bridge estimated Q3 Supply Chain Solutions revenue at “~$2,750M.”

surprises.description: Supply Chain Solutions operating profit was $274 million, below the preview’s roughly $289 million estimate, and its implied margin was about 9.1%, below the preview’s 10–11% guide range. The prior-year comparison also included a $330 million sale-leaseback gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Supply Chain Solutions ... operating profit of $274 million faces a tough comparison against a $330 million sale-leaseback gain in Q3 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated SCS operating profit at “~$289M” and listed its Q3 margin guidance as “10–11%.”

surprises.description: GAAP results included a $279 million net charge, including a $182 million Supply Chain Solutions goodwill impairment and $130 million of transformation costs. The preview centered its earnings expectations on adjusted EPS and did not flag these charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP results included a net charge of $279 million ($0.32 per share), comprising $130 million in transformation costs and a $182 million goodwill impairment in Supply Chain Solutions, partly offset by a $33 million MD-11 asset sale gain.”
